title: Daylight on the Longer Ridge
story: A rockfall had closed the marked canyon path, and the group reached the barrier tape while dust still hung in the air. The ranger post was two hours back, and the radio had no signal between the walls. Cloud was filling the upper cleft, and a night on the canyon floor would mean cold rock and no water beyond what they carried. Sera proposed the old ridge, longer and exposed, but still in daylight if they left at once. It rejoined the marked route above the fall. She had last used that cairn the previous spring. Two people wanted to wait for a ranger. Sera pointed out that nobody knew they had chosen the canyon, so no rescue was already coming. They took the ridge and reached the cairn while the slope below was still visible. The choice added wind and distance. It also kept them out of a darkening canyon.

vocabulary.definition: A collapse of rock onto a path.
Something placed so people cannot pass.
A narrow opening or crack in the rock.
Open to wind and weather, with little shelter.
Met up with a route again.
A small pile of stones used as a marker.

quiz.question: Where did the old ridge meet the marked route again?
options: Above the fall
At the ranger post
On the canyon floor after dark
Back at the barrier tape
quiz.explanation: The ridge rejoined the marked route above the fall.
quiz.supportingSentence: It rejoined the marked route above the fall.

quiz.question: Why was a rescue not already coming to meet them?
options: No rescuer had been told they chose the canyon
The ranger post was closed for the whole year
The radio was already speaking with a rescue team
The falling rock had burned their only map
quiz.correctAnswer: No rescuer had been told they chose the canyon
quiz.explanation: Sera says nobody knew they had chosen the canyon, so no rescue was already coming.
quiz.supportingSentence: Sera pointed out that nobody knew they had chosen the canyon, so no rescue was already coming.

quiz.question: Why does waiting for a ranger carry a danger of its own?
options: Night in the canyon would be cold and short of water
The ridge path was shorter than the canyon route
Sera had never walked during daylight
The barrier tape led directly up to the cairn
quiz.correctAnswer: Night in the canyon would be cold and short of water
quiz.explanation: A night on the canyon floor would mean cold rock and no water beyond what they carried.
quiz.supportingSentence: Cloud was filling the upper cleft, and a night on the canyon floor would mean cold rock and no water beyond what they carried.

quiz.question: What does exposed mean in the description of the ridge?
options: Open to the weather, with little shelter
Closed by rocks that had just fallen
Hidden under the floor of the canyon
Kept only for rangers who carry radios
quiz.correctAnswer: Open to the weather, with little shelter
quiz.explanation: Sera calls the ridge longer and exposed, meaning open to the weather.
quiz.supportingSentence: Sera proposed the old ridge, longer and exposed, but still in daylight if they left at once.

quiz.question: Why does the writer mention the previous spring?
options: To show Sera had already used that cairn
To explain why the canyon was shut the year before
To prove the group had camped there all winter
To show a ranger shifted the tape in spring
quiz.correctAnswer: To show Sera had already used that cairn
quiz.explanation: She had last used that cairn the previous spring, so the meeting point is known to her.
quiz.supportingSentence: She had last used that cairn the previous spring.
